clusters.title: Only one of D / L is read and the other, named in the words (D=, L=, dead, live, 'twice the dead load', 'each'), is silently taken as 0 + A load number is bound to the wrong kind or coefficient: a gap that crosses another load label, a number-first rule that binds across a label, an expression's first coefficient, a D/L slash pair read as a fraction, a substring test that hides a snow load, 'factored loads D=' not seen as factored
clusters.root_cause:
[load-pair-half-missing] reader.js fillAxialLoads lines 1457-1468: `if (d) B.set('D'...); if (l) B.set('L'...)` sets whichever kind was read and never asks for the other, although the text names it. The frozen engine's loadFromArgs then uses 0 (1.4D governs, Pu = 70 / 160 / 240 printed). FILL.loads_takedown line 2497 asks only when BOTH floor loads are missing (`if (!d && !l)`), so 'live load twice the dead load' becomes 0 (csel-06). The numbers are lost upstream in findLoads: the bare 'D = 50 k' rule (line 256-264) needs a load unit right after EACH number ('D=50 L=100 kips', 'D = 30, L = 60 kips', 'L=150', 'D = L = 75 kips'). The kind-named rule at 312 needs a unit ('dead 100 live 150 kips'). No rule reads 'twice / N times the dead load', 'L = 2D' or 'dead and live loads are each 50 kips'. Unitless numbers never reach the unused-number gate either. I checked this on the branch: 'D=50k L=100 kips' prints W8X18 (right).
[load-number-misbound] reader.js findLoads. (a) Line 236, the symbol form `... (?:=|:)\s*(N)(?:\s*-?\s*(UNITS)|(?![A-Za-z0-9]))`: the unitless branch accepts '1.2' in 'Pu = 1.2(100) + 1.6(150)' because '(' is not alphanumeric, so Pu = 1.2 kips is a given factored load ('adequate for Pu = 1.2'). (b) Line 258 / 312: in 'D/L = 200/300 kips' and 'dead/live = 80/50 psf' the '/' is a boundary, so only 'L = 200/300' / 'live = 80/50' match. N's fraction branch (line 87) turns them into 0.667 / 1.6, and D is lost. (c) The word-form gap at line 268 `[^0-9.;=]{0,28}?` runs from 'live load' across ' is twice the dead load of ' (csel-07) and takes the dead load's number as the live load. (d) The number-first rule at line 292 binds '80 psf live' across the label boundary in 'dead 80 psf live 100 psf'. Rule 312 then skips 'dead 80 psf' and 'live 100 psf' as overlaps, so D is missing and L = 80 (csel-08/09). The unused '100 psf' is then hidden across the chain by pipeline.js computeUnused 2463 / unusedOf 2619. (e) Rule 292 accepts only dead|live, so '50 k snow' is not read. readChunk's safety net (line ~2611, occ substring test) finds '50 k' inside '150 k live', so the number is not listed as unplaced (csel-24). (f) loadBasis line 1426 givenFactored misses 'factored loads D=200k L=300k' (a symbol stands between 'loads' and '='), so D and L are refactored (720 for 500; csel-11).
clusters.fix_plan:
[load-pair-half-missing] (1) Smallest safe guard, reader.js fillAxialLoads after line 1466: if exactly one of d/l was read and the text names the other kind, raise B.ask('load_L' or 'load_D', 'Your question names a live (dead) load but the page did not read its number. Type L (D) in kips.', ['L'] or ['D'], null, 'need'). Dead: `\b(?:P\s?_?)?D(?:L)?\s*=|\bdead\b`. Live: `\b(?:P\s?_?)?L(?:L)?\s*=(?![\d.\s\/]*(?:ft|feet|foot|in\b|'))|\blive\b`. Skip the ask when the words say the load is absent ('no live load', 'live load is zero', 'dead load only'). (2) The same in FILL.loads_takedown line 2497 for floor_D_psf / floor_L_psf (kind 'need'). (3) Coverage only where unambiguous, in findLoads: a bare pair sharing ONE trailing unit ('D=50 L=100 kips', 'D = 30, L = 60 kips': joined by space, comma or 'and', unit after the last) reads both in that unit. 'D = L = 75 kips' reads both as 75. 'dead and live loads are each 50 kips' reads both as 50. 'live load is twice / N times the dead load' gives L = N x D only when D was read with a unit. Anything else stays MISSING and goes to the ask, never 0. MUST NOT CHANGE: dead-load-only questions with no live word (XA-19, DS-21), 'L = 25 ft' (a length), L-shape names (L4x4), PD/PL symbols, a given factored Pu, takedowns that read both floor loads.
[load-number-misbound] reader.js only. (a) Line 236: reject the unitless branch when the number is followed by `\s*[(*x+]` or a second number. When 'Pu =' / 'P =' is followed by an arithmetic expression, raise B.ask('pu_formula', 'Your question writes the load as a formula: work it out and type Pu in kips.', ['Pu'], null, 'need'). ASK, no number in the message. (b) Lines 258/312: a slash pair of two symbols or two kinds ('D/L', 'dead/live') followed by a slash pair of two numbers is read in order (D = a, L = b, with the shared unit): ANSWER, because the order is unambiguous. Any other slash after a load symbol does not use the fraction branch; it stays MISSING and goes to the cluster load-pair-half-missing ask. (c) Line 268 gap: it may not cross another load-kind word or a load symbol with '=' or 'if': `(?:(?!\b(?:dead|live|snow|wind|rain|roof)\b|\b[DLSWPw]{1,2}\s*=|\bif\b)[^0-9.;=]){0,28}?`. The live load is then not read and the half-missing ask follows. (d) Line 292: skip a match whose number is directly preceded by a kind word (`(dead|live|snow|wind)\s*(?:=|:)?\s*$` on the slice before). Rule 312 then reads 'dead 80 psf' and 'live 100 psf': ANSWER 921.6 / 264. (e) Rule 292: add snow, so loads_combinations reads S = 50 (ANSWER 385 by the page's 7-combination form). In readChunk occ(): a match counts only when the character before it is not a digit or '.', so a missed load stays unplaced and blocking. (f) loadBasis: also `factored\s+loads?\s*,?\s*(?:[A-Za-z]{1,3}\s*=)` and '(factored)' / 'these are factored loads' give 'factored'. The existing loads_basis ask follows (ASK, not a silent sum). MUST NOT CHANGE: 'PD = 115 k', 'Pu = 800 kips', '100 k dead + 150 k live', the 'dead + live = 120 psf is a sum' guard, '3/4 in' fractions in bolt sizes, the framing-weight rule of C-28.

clusters.title: findBracing reads one brace with no axis, no negation, one height, and '1/3 points' as mid height, and fillColumn always puts it on the weak axis + Brace-is-a-pin segments get the whole column's end condition, a typed Ly with a fixed end takes the whole K, and printed per-axis K values are collapsed into one
clusters.root_cause:
[column-bracing-reading] reader.js findBracing lines 1844-1856. (a) Line 1846 (and the fallback at 1852) matches 'braced/bracing ... mid height' with no look at the words before ('not braced', 'un-') or after ('is removed'), so a negated brace sets fraction = 2 (ccap-272/207, csel-03). (b) No axis words are read: 'about its strong axis', 'about the x axis', 'in the plane of the web', 'strong axis only'. fillColumn 1943-1952 then always sets Ly = L/n and Lx = L. Only bothDir (1943) moves it to Lx (ccap-187/271/178, csel-04: 460.2 for 208.8). (c) Line 1849 `w = /third/ ? 3 : /quarter/ ? 4 : 2` turns '1/3 points' into mid height (ccap-309). (d) Only the first brace statement is read, so 'weak axis at third points and strong axis at mid height' loses the second (ccap-281). (e) Line 1853 exec()s the 'N ft above/from the base' regex once, so '10 ft and 20 ft from the base' keeps only 20 (ccap-280, csel-19). The useSeg split is then 20/10.
[column-segments-and-per-axis-K] reader.js fillColumn. The useSeg branch at lines 1954-1956 gives BOTH segments of a brace 'N ft above/from the base' `end_condition: eid` (the whole column's 'fixed-pinned' / 'fixed-fixed'). The her-method segRows builder (1912-1927) runs only from brace.fraction or 'segments of', never from brace.above (ccap-279: 823.6 for 721.5; ccap-257: 856.1 for 781.8). The builder is gated by `if (fx && !Ls.ly)` (1912), so a TYPED Ly with a fixed end skips it. fillEnds (1569-1570) then puts the column's K on the whole Ly (ccap-282). fillEnds lines 1555-1557: with no worded end, kEnds[0] (the FIRST printed K) is set into both x and y end conditions, and the second K and its 'about x / about y' words are ignored (ccap-276). fillEnds line 1531: a worded end wins and the printed K list is never compared with it (ccap-274). fillColumn's direct-K path (line 1896) is off whenever 2 K values or 'Kx =' are printed.
clusters.fix_plan:
[column-bracing-reading] reader.js findBracing + fillColumn 1943-1956. (a) Negation: 'not|no|never|without' within the clause before the match, a 'un-' prefix, or '(is|are|was|been) (removed|omitted|taken out|eliminated)' after it means NO brace: ANSWER with L about both axes (unambiguous: ccap-272/207 466, csel-03 W12X65). A text with both a negated and a positive brace raises an ASK (need). (b) Axis: read the axis words in the brace's own clause. strong|major|x[- ]?axis|x-x|'in the plane of the web' gives 'x', so Lx = L/n and Ly = L (ANSWER 208.8 / 437.4, W14X90). weak|minor|y|'weak direction' or no axis word keeps the current Ly = L/n. 'both' keeps bothDir. Unclear words ('strong direction', 'perpendicular to the web') raise an ASK. (c) '1\/3' gives third and '1\/4' gives quarter (ANSWER 716). (d) Loop over every brace statement: two statements naming different axes set each axis (ccap-281: Ly = L/3, Lx = L/2: 764.0). Two statements for the same axis, or one that cannot be placed, raise an ASK. (e) Collect every 'N ft (and M ft) from/above the base|bottom'. Two or more heights on a pinned-pinned column give segments at those heights (brace = pin, her method; ANSWER 744.7 / W14X99). With a fixed end, use cluster column-segments-and-per-axis-K. Unclear raises an ASK. MUST NOT CHANGE: plain 'braced at mid-height' (Ly = L/2), 'about the weak axis at mid height', 'in both directions/axes', 'braced against sidesway' (an end condition, not a mid brace), HW 5-17 'segments of 12, 8 and 8 ft', the 9/9 class column at third points.
[column-segments-and-per-axis-K] reader.js only. (1) useSeg branch 1954-1956: build the end conditions as segRows does (a brace is a pin). The segment that touches a fixed end keeps 'fixed-pinned' and the other is 'pinned-pinned'. With 'fixed at both ends' each segment is fixed-pinned. When it is not said which end is fixed (fx.guessed), ASK. This ANSWERs ccap-279 721.5 and ccap-257 781.8 by her method. (2) Line 1912: a typed Ly on a column with a fixed end has two readings (Ly is a braced segment, a pin at the brace, versus the whole column's K), so ASK (need: 'the end condition of the weak-axis segment'). Never the whole K silently (ccap-282). (3) fillEnds / fillColumn K path: if every printed K is tied to an axis by its own words ('K = 0.8 about x', 'Kx = 1.0', 'Ky = 0.8'), set KLx_ft = Kx x Lx and KLy_ft = Ky x Ly directly with the arithmetic shown (unambiguous; ccap-276: 466.6, and ccap-277 in cluster form-choice-guards). Otherwise ASK. A printed K that disagrees with a worded end condition raises an ASK naming both, never one silently (ccap-274). MUST NOT CHANGE: the single printed K path (review 4: KL = K x L), HW 5-17 segments 12/8/8, the 9/9 third-point column, the cover line 'K = 1.0 for all columns', end conditions said per axis ('Lx = 15 ft (fixed at both ends), Ly = ...').

clusters.title: Column takedown: floor count not read ('3floors', 'stories'), 'N story' plus a roof, per-floor kips taken as the total, the level asked ('below the roof', 'between floors'), two bay sizes, (b) carrying (a)'s Pu
clusters.root_cause: [takedown-floors-and-levels] (a) reader.js gatherFacts floorsN line 747 `(WN)\s+(?:floor|story|storey)(?:s)?` needs a space ('3floors') and does not match 'stories'. With no count the finder falls to loads_factored and prints 'Factored load: 176 psf' as the column load (csel-22/23). (b) Line 747 / FILL.loads_takedown 2481: 'a 4 story building' becomes floors = 4 below the roof, even when the roof is loaded separately (roof + 3 floors is the other reading; csel-16). (c) FILL.loads_factored (2505) and fillAxialLoads (1438) never look at F.floorsN, so 'the load from each floor is D = 120 k' becomes the total (csel-14). computeUnused 2463 drops the count. (d) pipeline.js markLevel 3020-3028 has no 'below/under the roof' and no 'between the 2nd and 3rd floors', so the base load is printed (csel-17/18). (e) loads_takedown line 2468 `bay.exec(t)` takes the first 'bays A x B' and ignores the second bay (csel-15). (f) pipeline carryAcross step 2 (3464-3482) carries Pu_bottom from (a)'s takedown into (b)'s column_select, although (b) names its own floor count (csel-13).
clusters.fix_plan: [takedown-floors-and-levels] (a) reader.js line 747: `(WN)\s*(?:floor|stor(?:y|ies|eys?))(?:s)?` (glued and 'stories'). This is a coverage fix: the existing takedown then answers or asks. Check that no '3floors' look-alike turns into a count in the regression. (b) 'N story/storey building' plus loads given for the roof gives an ASK on 'floors' (need) with both readings. (c) fillAxialLoads / loads_factored: a load given 'from/for each floor' or 'per floor', with a floor count in the words, gives an ASK (need: the total or the takedown). Never one floor as the total. (d) markLevel: add `(?:just\s+)?(?:below|under|beneath)\s+the\s+roof`, `between\s+the\s+\w+\s+and\s+(?:the\s+)?\w+\s+(?:floors?|levels?|stor)`, and 'from the Nth floor to the roof'. Each gives the existing STOP sentence. (e) loads_takedown: two 'bays A x B' sizes for an interior column give an ASK for tributary_area_sf (need), never the first bay. (f) carryAcross step 2: do not carry into a part whose own text has a floor count or any load (ASK). MUST NOT CHANGE: '3 floors' / 'four office floors' takedowns, the roof-sentence logic of 0.6, the existing markLevel stops, the 'A column supports a single floor ... 900 ft2' floor-to-column route, C-28's framing-weight rule.
